why: the cohort section only, withdrawn on 2026-09-23 by TOFU-529 and by this file rather than by an edit to the report. The reader that produced those counts tagged its fields with the older capitalized spellings only, so it decoded 51 of the 58 single file sessions to all zero and classified each of them as predating cache accounting. The shared reader handles both spellings, and on the same corpus the usable turns rise from 51 to 97 and the turns carrying a cache write from 24 to 38. Every count, dollar and percentage in that section was computed over a sample less than half the size it should have been, so the figures fall. The verdict does not: the schema block is still written to cache once and read back on every later step, and the corrected sample makes that stronger rather than weaker. The headline figure of 16,575 bytes and 4,143 tokens is measured from the wire encoder rather than the corpus and stands unchanged, as does the single turn measured in full.
fell: The same pattern holds across every recorded turn old enough to carry cache fields. 51 of 111 turns under .tofu/sessions carry usable cache accounting (the other 60 predate cache accounting or hold no steps, see the skip counts below); of those, 24 had at least one cache-write step, and 23 of those 24 ran a second model call and so read the write back at least once. Restricted to the 15 turns whose first write is at today's 18-tool scale, 14 of 15 ran a second call.

Over the 24 turns with a cache write, the cohort billed 103777 fresh input tokens, 675237 cache-write tokens and 5700621 cache-read tokens: 88.0% of everything billed across this whole sample was a cache read.

The one case where deferring would pay is a turn that makes exactly one model call and never returns for a second, which was 1 of 24 turns in this sample: too rare and too cheap a miss to build a mechanism for.
